answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no added delivery risk at 94% utilization with zero buffer, while still chasing the 18% spend cut. The incumbent refused a mid-cycle reopen, but this is a 14-day renewal cliff with a competing quote already in hand; memory_c4 and memory_c6 say renewal-point benchmarking and multi-year structure have moved this incumbent on price without a vendor change, and memory_c1 says staying put protected integration and deliveries. Switching primary would meet the mandate on price alone but would raise onboarding/delivery risk on a line with no buffer, violating the objective. Deferral is unsafe because the contract does not auto-renew. Single decision: negotiate renewal terms against the market quote and keep the incumbent for continuity. Verifying memory_c4 because it is the load-bearing claim that renewal negotiation still works after a refusal; outcome of that negotiation remains uncertain and a failed talk plus expiry would hit the line.
